newsitem.title: FRANCE: French franc, stocks fall on EU budget pact delay.
newsitem.headline: French franc, stocks fall on EU budget pact delay.

text.p: The French franc and stocks fell on Monday after the new Socialist-led government called for a "period of consultation" on a pact limiting budget deficits of countries that join a single European currency.

The Paris Bourse opened higher but slid to 2.2 percent down on Friday's close amid worries over the future of European economic and monetary union, dealers said. The franc fell by more than half a centime to 3.3827 to the deutschemark.

Diplomats said Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told European Union ministers in Luxembourg that Prime Minister Lionel Jospin wanted to inform the National Assembly about the pact on June 19, two days after an EU summit was supposed to have approved the agreement in Amsterdam.
The news caused an instant slip in both French shares and bonds.
"It's down on the French position on the stability pact, the fact the French cannot agree to the stability pact today," a German bank economist in London said.

He said the new left-wing French government's determination to seek an employment component in addition to the budget stability pact was "negative for the EMU process" and increased the risk that Germany may not go ahead with the single currency.
